UnitStatement: The Contribution Review Checklist is a project-governance intake record for public repository contributions.
The checklist is not legal advice, professional engineering approval, certification, sealing, standards-body endorsement, or a code-compliance claim.

Use the checklist before accepting contributions that add or modify public data, examples, report templates, benchmark cases, import fixtures, documentation excerpts, rule-pack examples, component/material/library records, or generated artifacts that may expose private or protected content.
This draft checklist is aligned to execution/_Decomposition/SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md revision 0.7 and approved DAG-006 coordination authority.
The project license has been selected as PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0.
The checklist records contribution-source rights and redistribution evidence separately from the project license notice.

The final contributor legal mechanism, maintainer roster/quorum, release authority, legal-review authority, security contact, release-label vocabulary, human-acceptance workflow, and jurisdiction-specific professional-practice wording remain TBD until recorded by the human project authority or qualified reviewer.

The Contribution Identity section records review ID, contribution title, contributor, reviewer, related deliverable/issue/PR, changed paths, contribution type, project license notice, contributor certification record, and review date.
Allowed contribution-type values are code, schema, documentation, example, benchmark, data, template, and other.
The default contributor certification record is governance/CONTRIBUTOR_CERTIFICATION_TEMPLATE.md or equivalent.

The Source And Rights Evidence section records source name, source location, source type, source license/redistribution basis, contributor certification, certification-statement acceptance, redistribution status, and evidence attachment/note.
Allowed source-type values are invented, original, public_domain, permissive_license, private_user_supplied, proprietary_with_permission, unknown, and protected_suspected.
Allowed redistribution-status values are public_permissive, private_only, unknown, protected_suspected, and rejected.
Acceptance requires a recorded source, redistribution basis, contributor certification, and reviewer disposition.
Contributions with unknown, protected_suspected, or missing evidence cannot be accepted as public data.

Use governance/CONTRIBUTOR_CERTIFICATION_TEMPLATE.md for the default contributor certification record unless a maintainer-approved form preserves the same source, rights, redistribution, protected-content, private-data, and review fields.
The Protected-Content Screen verifies no standards-body code text, commentary, figures, or examples are copied into public content.
The Protected-Content Screen verifies no copied material allowable tables, SIF tables, flexibility-factor tables, or protected dimensional/rating tables are included.
The Protected-Content Screen verifies no copied commercial software examples, report templates, benchmark files, or proprietary formulas are included without permission.
The Protected-Content Screen verifies no proprietary vendor catalog data is included without documented redistribution rights.
The Protected-Content Screen verifies public examples use invented, original, public-domain, or permissively licensed values only.
The Protected-Content Screen verifies documentation excerpts are original summaries or permissively licensed quotations within project policy.
Allowed screen result values are pass, fail, pending, not_applicable, and escalated.
The Private-Data Screen verifies no private project model, owner standard, company design basis, or client data is included.
The Private-Data Screen verifies no private material, component, rule-pack, allowable, SIF, flexibility, or load-combination data is included.
The Private-Data Screen verifies telemetry, issue logs, screenshots, and reports exclude private engineering data by default.
The Private-Data Screen verifies private-only content is stored outside public examples and marked private-only where referenced.
The Engineering And Product-Claim Screen verifies no claim of professional engineering approval, certification, sealing, authentication, or code compliance for reliance.
The Engineering And Product-Claim Screen verifies no standards-body endorsement or official approval claim.
The Engineering And Product-Claim Screen verifies missing engineering values remain TBD or explicit findings rather than defaults.
The Engineering And Product-Claim Screen verifies mechanics results, user rule checks, and human acceptance remain distinct.

The Tests And Evidence section records required tests/scans run, protected-content scan result, schema/provenance validation result, contributor certification template review, documentation review result, and explicit deferrals.
The Disposition section records review disposition, disposition rationale, required follow-up, human/legal escalation need, and approving maintainer/authority.
Allowed review-disposition values are pending, accepted, rejected, quarantined, private_only, escalated, and TBD.
A contribution may be marked accepted only when source rights, protected-content risk, private-data risk, and product-claim review are closed or explicitly deferred by a recorded maintainer decision.
Complete the Quarantine Record section when any protected or private content risk is unresolved.
The Quarantine Record section records quarantine status, quarantine path, issue/decision record, escalation owner, and resolution.
Allowed quarantine-status values are not_required, required, complete, and TBD.
The default quarantine path is quarantine/protected-content/ or a maintainer-approved equivalent.
Quarantined material must not be copied into public examples, converted into public defaults, or used as public fixture data while the review remains unresolved.
